q.s: Harappa, the first Indus Valley site to be excavated, lies on the bank of which river?
q.x: Harappa lies in Sahiwal (Montgomery) district of Pakistani Punjab on the left bank of the Ravi; Mohenjodaro is on the Indus.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT in present-day Pakistan?
q.x: Lothal is in Gujarat, India; Harappa, Mohenjodaro (Larkana) and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan.

q.s: Who announced the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilisation to the world in 1924?
q.x: John Marshall, Director-General of the ASI, announced the discovery in 1924 and coined the term "Indus Valley Civilisation"; Sahni and Banerji were the excavators of Harappa and Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as the best evidence of social differentiation in Harappan society?
o: Variation in burial goods and ornaments
q.x: Differences in grave goods and quality of ornaments best show social differentiation; uniform bricks show standardisation, and no temples, palaces or proof of rigid caste have been found.

q.s: Which of the following has NOT been found in Harappan cities?
q.x: No temples or palaces have been found; granaries, barracks at Harappa and drains have.

q.s: The bronze chariot group along with buffalo, rhinoceros and elephant figures was found at:
q.x: The Daimabad hoard (Maharashtra) contains the bronze chariot, buffalo, rhinoceros and elephant; the copper dog and bird come from Lothal.

q.s: In the Rigveda, the word 'gotra' originally meant:
q.x: In the Rigveda gotra meant a cowpen; its sense of lineage appears first in the Atharvaveda, so gotra exogamy was not yet established.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the centre of Aryan culture shifted from Punjab to the:
q.x: The Later Vedic people moved from Punjab into the Ganga-Yamuna Doab (Kuru-Panchala) and then towards Kosala, Kashi and Videha by about 600 BCE.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a site of the Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)?
q.x: NBPW (c. 700–200 BCE) sites are mainly in the Ganga valley such as Hastinapur, Kaushambi, Rajgir and Pataliputra; Lothal is a Harappan port.

q.s: In the Ganga valley, Northern Black Polished Ware succeeded which pottery tradition?
q.x: NBPW, the pottery of the Second Urbanisation, came after the Painted Grey Ware of the Later Vedic period.

q.s: Who founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891?
q.x: The Maha Bodhi Society was founded in 1891 by the Sri Lankan Buddhist Anagarika Dharmapala; Cunningham was an archaeologist.

q.s: Which of the following Ashtamahasthanas is NOT in India?
q.x: Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, is in Nepal.

q.s: Pradyota, a contemporary of Mahavira and the Buddha, ruled over:
q.x: Pradyota ruled Avanti (capital Ujjain); Prasenajit ruled Kosala and Ajatashatru Magadha.

q.s: Which of the following rulers was NOT a contemporary of Mahavira?
q.x: Ashoka ruled in the 3rd century BCE; the others were 6th-5th century BCE contemporaries.

q.s: Which edict of Ashoka names the Andhras among the peoples within his domain?
q.x: Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples following Dhamma within the empire.

q.s: The Satavahanas began their political career as feudatories of the:
q.x: The Satavahanas rose after the decline of the Mauryas, whose feudatories they had been.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the end of the Mauryas is correct?
o: Pushyamitra's two Ashvamedhas are mentioned in Dhanadeva's Ayodhya inscription.
Brihadratha was the immediate successor of Ashoka.
The Sunga dynasty was founded around 232 BC.
Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmana of the Kashyapa gotra.
q.x: Brihadratha was the seventh king after Ashoka; the Sungas came around 187 BC (232 BC is Ashoka's death), and Pushyamitra was of the Bharadvaja gotra.

q.s: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
q.x: Brihadratha, the seventh king after Ashoka, was killed by his commander Pushyamitra Sunga, who founded the Sunga dynasty around 187 BC.

q.s: The Milindapanha is a dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and the monk:
q.x: The Milindapanha (Questions of Milinda) records Menander's discussion with the Buddhist monk Nagasena.

q.s: The capital of the Indo-Greek king Menander was:
q.x: Menander ruled from Sakala (modern Sialkot), not Taxila.

q.s: Mauryan pillars were made from monolithic shafts of polished:
q.x: The Mauryan pillars are monolithic, highly polished shafts of Chunar sandstone standing as independent monuments.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Mauryan pillars?
o: They formed parts of larger buildings
A bell-shaped inverted lotus lies below the abacus
q.x: The pillars are independent monuments, not parts of architectural structures.

q.s: The ancient university of Nalanda was destroyed by:
q.x: Nalanda was sacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji at the end of the 12th century.

q.s: The site of Nalanda was identified in 1861 by:
q.x: Alexander Cunningham, the first Director of the ASI, identified Nalanda in 1861.

q.s: Charaka, the author of Charaka Samhita, was the court physician of:
q.x: Charaka was physician to Kanishka; Jivaka served Bimbisara and Dhanvantari was at the court of Chandragupta II.

q.s: Jivaka, the famous physician of the Buddha's time, served at the court of:
q.x: Jivaka was the royal physician of Bimbisara of Magadha.

q.s: Pulakesin II defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the river:
q.x: Pulakesin II of the Badami Chalukyas stopped Harsha on the Narmada and took the title Paramesvara.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of Pulakesin II?
o: He defeated Harsha on the Narmada
His victory is recorded in the Aihole inscription
He belonged to the Rashtrakuta dynasty
q.x: Pulakesin II was a Chalukya of Badami; the Rashtrakutas later replaced the Chalukyas.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
q.x: Harshacharita is Banabhatta's biography of Harsha; Nagananda, Ratnavali and Priyadarshika are Harsha's own plays.

q.s: The Chalukyas of Badami were overthrown in the mid-eighth century by the:
q.x: Dantidurga's Rashtrakutas replaced the Badami Chalukyas around 753 CE, ending the Chalukya-Pallava rivalry.

q.s: Which Pallava king captured Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title 'Vatapikonda'?
q.x: Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi in 642 CE; the Chalukyas under Vikramaditya I recovered it about 13 years later.

q.s: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194), Muhammad Ghori defeated:
q.x: Ghori beat Prithviraj at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192) and Jaichand of Kannauj at Chandawar (1194).

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Muhammad Ghori?
q.x: Khatoli (1517) was fought between Rana Sanga and Ibrahim Lodi.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a village-level functionary in the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: The shiqdar headed a shiq (district); the patwari, muqaddam and khut worked at the village level.

q.s: Which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate had NOT been a slave?
q.x: Aibak, Iltutmish and Balban had been slaves (bandagan), hence the name 'Slave' or 'Mamluk' dynasty; Razia was Iltutmish's daughter.

q.s: In which language did Ibn Battuta write his travel account, the Rihla?
q.x: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta wrote the Rihla in Arabic.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as his envoy in 1342 to:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and in 1342 sent him as envoy to China.

q.s: Where is the Mughal emperor Babur finally buried?
q.x: Babur died at Agra in 1530 but his body was later moved to Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul.

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: Haldighati (1576) was fought between Akbar's forces and Maharana Pratap.

q.s: Under the Mughals, land whose revenue went directly to the imperial treasury was called:
q.x: Khalisa was crown land; a jagir gave only the right to collect revenue, and suyurghal was a charitable revenue-free grant.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a category of land or grant under the Mughals?
q.x: Zabti was a system of revenue assessment (measurement), not a category of land; khalisa, jagir and suyurghal were.

q.s: Where was Dara Shikoh buried after his execution by Aurangzeb?
q.x: Dara Shikoh, betrayed by Malik Jiwan, was buried in Humayun's Tomb.

q.s: After his defeat in the War of Succession, Shah Shuja fled to:
q.x: Shah Shuja, governor of Bengal, fled to Arakan, where he perished.

q.s: In medieval Indian trade, a 'hundi' was a:
q.x: Hundis were bills of exchange issued by shroffs; bima was insurance of goods in transit.

q.s: In medieval Indian trade, the term 'bima' referred to:
q.x: Bima was the insurance of goods in transit.

q.s: During the Mughal period, the Chettis were the dominant merchants of the:
q.x: The Chettis dominated the Coromandel coast while Muslim (Mappila) merchants dominated Malabar.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Marwari merchant community of Rajasthan?
q.x: Oswals, Maheshwaris and Agarwals were Marwaris; the Chettis were merchants of the Coromandel coast.

q.s: Sirr-i-Akbar of Dara Shikoh is a Persian translation of the:
q.x: Sirr-i-Akbar translates fifty Upanishads into Persian; it reached Europe through Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version.

q.s: Dara Shikoh was a disciple of Miyan Mir of which Sufi order?
q.x: Dara Shikoh was a Qadiri Sufi and disciple of Miyan Mir of Lahore.

q.s: Mantralayam, which has the samadhi of Raghavendra Swami, is in which district?
q.x: Mantralayam on the Tungabhadra is in Kurnool district.

q.s: The Bhadrachalam temple is associated with which devotee?
q.x: Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) built the Bhadrachalam temple; Annamacharya is linked with Tirumala.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sufism is correct?
o: Sufism rejected the need for a spiritual guide (pir).
Sufism had no influence on the Bhakti saints.
Sufism kept away from the local languages of India.
Sufism valued inner spiritual experience over formal Shariat observance.
q.x: Sufism, like Bhakti, stressed inner devotion over formal ritual; it relied on the pir-murid bond and used local languages, and its meeting with Bhakti produced a composite culture.

q.s: The dargah of Baba Farid is located at:
q.x: Baba Farid's dargah is at Ajodhan (Pakpattan); Bakhtiyar Kaki lies at Mehrauli, Salim Chishti at Fatehpur Sikri and Burhanuddin Gharib at Khuldabad.

q.s: Which of the following saint–dargah pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Salim Chishti's dargah is at Fatehpur Sikri.

q.s: Goa, Daman and Diu were freed from Portuguese rule in 1961 through:
q.x: Operation Vijay freed Goa, Daman and Diu on 19 December 1961; Operation Polo was the Hyderabad action of 1948.

q.s: Petapoli, a Portuguese and Dutch trading centre on the Andhra coast, is the old name of:
q.x: Petapoli is Nizampatnam in present Bapatla district.

q.s: The Inam Commission of 1852, which confiscated many estates before 1857, worked in the:
q.x: The Inam Commission (1852) of the Bombay Presidency confiscated thousands of estates, adding to discontent before 1857.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, the 15-member Council of India advised the:
q.x: The Council of India advised the Secretary of State, who was responsible to Parliament.

q.s: The Council of India set up in 1858 was abolished by the:
q.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the Council of India.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a term of the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) with Shah Alam II?
o: The Company got the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
The Company was to pay Rs 26 lakh a year
Shah Alam received Kora and Allahabad
q.x: Banaras was left to Balwant Singh; Shah Alam got Kora, Allahabad and Rs 26 lakh a year and became the Company's pensioner.

q.s: Who stopped the Rs 26 lakh payment to Shah Alam II and sold Kora and Allahabad to the Nawab of Awadh?
q.x: Warren Hastings, Governor of Bengal from 1772, stopped the payment and sold the two districts to Awadh.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT done by Warren Hastings?
o: Obtaining the Diwani of Bengal in 1765
Stopping the tribute to Shah Alam II
Selling Kora and Allahabad to Awadh
q.x: The Diwani was obtained by Clive in 1765; the rest were Hastings's acts.

q.s: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa was granted to the East India Company in 1765 by:
q.x: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani after the Battle of Buxar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Company's affairs before 1773 is correct?
o: The Diwani of 1765 was granted by Shuja-ud-Daula.
The Select Committee of 1772 on Company affairs was headed by Burgoyne.
The Act of 1767 made the Company pay £400,000 a year to the Mughal emperor.
In 1767 the Company's dividend was capped at 12 per cent.
q.x: The Diwani came from Shah Alam II; the £400,000 went to the British treasury, and the dividend cap was 10 per cent.

q.s: The first printing press in India was set up at Goa in 1556 by the:
q.x: Portuguese Jesuits set up India's first press at Goa in 1556.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the early press in India is correct?
o: Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780) was a Bengali weekly.
The first printing press in India was set up at Calcutta.
Rammohan Roy closed Mirat-ul-Akhbar in protest against the Licensing Regulations of 1823.
q.x: Hicky's paper was in English, the first press was at Goa (1556), and Mirat-ul-Akhbar was a Persian weekly.

q.s: Which city had the first Municipal Corporation in India?
q.x: The Madras Municipal Corporation was set up in 1688.

q.s: Who is called the Father of Local Self-Government in India?
q.x: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 earned him the title.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: Voting on the budget as a whole
q.x: Members could discuss the budget and move resolutions but could not vote on it as a whole; the Act brought indirect elections, separate electorates and non-official majorities in the provinces.

q.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
q.x: The League was founded at Dacca in December 1906; it preached loyalty to the British and did not oppose the partition of Bengal.

q.s: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh was founded at Nagpur in 1925 by:
q.x: K.B. Hedgewar founded the RSS at Nagpur in 1925; Golwalkar was his successor.

q.s: At which Congress session (1921) did Hasrat Mohani move the demand for complete independence?
q.x: Hasrat Mohani and Swami Kumarananda moved the complete-independence demand at the Ahmedabad session of 1921; it was adopted only at Lahore in 1929.

q.s: After the 1937 elections, the Congress ministry in the North-West Frontier Province was headed by:
q.x: Dr Khan Sahib, brother of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, led the NWFP ministry; Sikandar Hayat Khan led Punjab and Fazlul Huq Bengal.

q.s: In which of the following provinces did the Congress NOT form a ministry in 1937?
q.x: Bengal had Fazlul Huq's coalition ministry; Congress formed ministries in Bombay, Madras, Bihar and others.

q.s: The Atmiya Sabha was founded in 1815 by:
q.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1815; Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839.

q.s: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 at:
q.x: The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang with Keshab Chandra Sen's inspiration.

q.s: The first Adi-Andhra session (Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha) of 1917 was held at:
q.x: The 1917 session met at Vijayawada; the second conference (1919) met at Machilipatnam and the first Adi-Andhra Sadassu (1921) at Amalapuram.

q.s: Karunalayam (1909), an orphanage in Andhra, was founded by the:
q.x: Karunalayam was founded by the Pithapuram Raja; Chilakamarti founded the Ram Mohan Roy School in 1909.

q.s: The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established in 1901 at:
q.x: The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam, a pioneer Telugu library, was set up at Hyderabad in 1901.

q.s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911 during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The annulment was announced at the 1911 Durbar under Lord Hardinge II; Curzon, who partitioned Bengal, left in 1905.

q.s: Which British sovereign personally attended the Delhi Durbar of 1911?
q.x: The 1911 Durbar was the only one attended by the reigning sovereign, George V.

q.s: Which leader was deported to Mandalay in 1907 along with Ajit Singh?
q.x: Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay in 1907; Pal was jailed for refusing to testify against Aurobindo.

q.s: Who is called the 'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts' in India?
q.x: Bipin Chandra Pal is called the Father of Revolutionary Thoughts; Aurobindo was called the Prophet of Indian Nationalism.

q.s: M.N. Roy founded the emigre Communist Party of India in 1920 at:
q.x: M.N. Roy founded the CPI (emigre group) at Tashkent in 1920; he also founded the Communist Party of Mexico.

q.s: Which of the following statements about M.N. Roy is correct?
o: He founded the CPI at Moscow in 1920.
He brought out the journal Talwar from Berlin.
He founded the Communist Party of Mexico.
q.x: Roy founded the CPI at Tashkent, his paper was the Vanguard (Talwar was Chattopadhyaya's), and he founded the Radical Democratic Party (1940).

q.s: The first president of the All India Kisan Sabha, formed at Lucknow in 1936, was:
q.x: Sahajanand Saraswati was president and N.G. Ranga general secretary of the AIKS formed in April 1936.

q.s: N.G. Ranga served as the first general secretary of the:
q.x: N.G. Ranga was the general secretary of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936).

q.s: The slogan "Simon Go Back" was coined by:
q.x: Yusuf Meherally coined the slogan during the boycott of the Simon Commission.

q.s: Which of the following parties did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
q.x: The Justice Party stayed out of the boycott; the Congress, Hindu Mahasabha and Jinnah's League joined it.

q.s: Which of the following institutions was NOT founded during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
q.x: Jamia Millia (1920), Gujarat Vidyapith (1920) and Kashi Vidyapith (1921) were national institutions of the movement; BHU was founded in 1916.

q.s: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 at:
q.x: Jamia Millia Islamia began at Aligarh in 1920 and later moved to Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT a Swarajist?
q.x: Vallabhbhai Patel was a No-changer; Das, Motilal Nehru and Vithalbhai Patel were Swarajists.

q.s: The Swarajists wanted to enter the legislative councils in order to:
o: Obstruct and 'end or mend' them from within
q.x: The Swarajists planned to wreck the councils from within by obstruction; the No-changers opposed council entry.

q.s: The Communal Award was announced by Ramsay MacDonald in the year:
q.x: The Communal Award came in August 1932, after the Nehru Report (1928) and the Karachi session (1931).

q.s: The Karachi session of 1931, which adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights, was presided over by:
q.x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi session of March 1931.

q.s: The Ashoka Chakra in the National Flag is taken from the:
q.x: The 24-spoke Chakra comes from Ashoka's Sarnath Lion Capital; it replaced the charkha.

q.s: Under the Flag Code, the ratio of the length to the width of the National Flag is:
q.x: The National Flag adopted on 22 July 1947 has a length-to-width ratio of 3 : 2.

q.s: Bardoli taluk, the scene of the 1928 satyagraha led by Vallabhbhai Patel, is in which district?
q.x: Bardoli is in Surat district; Kheda was the scene of the 1918 satyagraha.

q.s: Which inquiry reduced the Bardoli revenue increase to about 6 per cent?
q.x: The Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry cut the hike of about 30 per cent down to about 6 per cent.

q.s: Zamindari estates in the Andhra area were abolished by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act of:
q.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 abolished zamindaris; the Telangana Inams Abolition Act came in 1955.

q.s: The A.P. Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 adopted which unit for fixing the ceiling?
q.x: Following the 1972 national guidelines of the Central Land Reforms Committee, the 1973 Act took the family as the unit.

q.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949 at:
q.x: The Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada in 1949; it held its first session at Warangal (1950) and second at Hyderabad (1954).

q.s: Langhnaj, an important Mesolithic site, is located in:
q.x: Langhnaj is in Gujarat; Bagor is the well-known Mesolithic site of Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mesolithic sites is correct?
o: Lekhahia and Baghai Khor are rock shelters of the Vindhyas.
Chopani Mando is in the Son valley.
q.x: Langhnaj is in Gujarat, Paisra in Bihar (Munger) and Chopani Mando in the Belan valley.

q.s: Which inscription calls Gautamiputra Satakarni 'Ekabrahmana'?
q.x: The Nasik Prasasti of his mother Gautami Balasri calls him Ekabrahmana and Varnasankarya-nirodhaka.

q.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated which Kshaharata ruler?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni destroyed the Kshaharata line of Nahapana and restruck his coins.

q.s: Which of the following dynasties used Telugu as its official language?
q.x: Telugu became the official language under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi; the Satavahanas used Prakrit and the Salankayanas Sanskrit.

q.s: The first Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India was issued by the Ikshvaku ruler:
q.x: Ehuvala's Swarna Devalayam inscription (11th regnal year) at Nagarjunakonda is the first Sanskrit inscription of South India.

q.s: From the 4th century CE, the language of inscriptions in Andhra shifted:
q.x: Sanskrit replaced Prakrit in inscriptions from the 4th century CE.

q.s: The greatest ruler of the Renati Cholas was:
q.x: Punyakumara (c. 625–650), husband of Vasantapori, was the greatest Renati Chola ruler.

q.s: The Musunuri Nayakas, who freed coastal Andhra from Tughlaq rule, were led by:
q.x: Prolaya Nayaka and his cousin Kapaya Nayaka founded Musunuri rule (1325–1368).

q.s: Which of the following dynasty–founder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Gajapatis were founded by Kapilendra (1435); Singama founded the Recherla Velamas.

q.s: Rudramadevi of the Kakatiya dynasty was married to:
o: Veerabhadra of the Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas
q.x: Rudramadevi married Veerabhadra of the Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas; her sister Ganapamba married the Kota chief.

q.s: Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to:
q.x: Tikkana dedicated it to Manumasiddhi II of Nellore, whom Ganapatideva restored at Tikkana's request.

q.s: In 1263 the Kakatiyas were defeated at Muttukur near Nellore by:
q.x: Jatavarman Sundara Pandya won at Muttukur in 1263 and Nellore fell to the Pandyas.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, the gold coin was known as the:
q.x: The Mada or Gadyana was gold, the Ruka silver, and Visa, Adduga and Padika smaller units.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Kakatiya coin?
q.x: The tanka was the Delhi Sultanate coin; Ruka, Visa and Padika were Kakatiya denominations.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, 'Pullari' was a tax on:
q.x: Pullari was the grazing tax; Dari Sunkam was a road toll and Angadi Sunkam a weekly-market tax.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Kakatiya tax?
q.x: Jizya was a tax of Muslim states on non-Muslims; the others were Kakatiya levies.

q.s: The city of Ahmedabad on the Sabarmati was founded in 1411 by:
q.x: Ahmad Shah I founded Ahmedabad in 1411; Zafar Khan (Muzaffar Shah I) founded the Gujarat Sultanate in 1407.

q.s: Which Gujarat sultan captured Girnar and Champaner?
q.x: Mahmud Begarha took Girnar and Champaner and joined Egypt against the Portuguese.

q.s: The Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara was founded by:
q.x: Vira Narasimha replaced the Saluvas and began Tuluva rule; Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangamas and Tirumala began the Aravidu line.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a dynasty of the Vijayanagara empire?
q.x: The four Vijayanagara dynasties were Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu; the Bahmanis were their rivals.

q.s: The Chola emperor Kulottunga I was the son of:
q.x: Kulottunga I was the son of the Eastern Chalukya Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi; Vimaladitya was his grandfather.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Kulottunga I is correct?
o: The Kalingattuparani about him was written by Kambar.
Kulottunga Cholapuram is the old name of Machilipatnam.
He took the Vengi throne in 1075 after the death of Vijayaditya VII.
He was the son of Vimaladitya and Kundavai.
q.x: The Kalingattuparani is by Jayamkondar, Kulottunga Cholapuram was Visakhapatnam, and he was the son of Rajaraja Narendra.

q.s: The capital of the Velanati Chodas was:
q.x: The Velanati Chodas ruled from Chandavolu (Dhanadapuram); Gonka II was their greatest ruler.

q.s: Before shifting to Warangal, the capital of the Kakatiyas was:
q.x: The Kakatiyas ruled first from Anamakonda (Hanumakonda) and then Warangal; Rekapalli was the Musunuri seat.

q.s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Musunuri seat was Rekapalli; Mahishmathi was the Anupa capital.

q.s: Under Company rule, the Guntur region turned to the cultivation of which commercial crop?
q.x: The demand for cash revenue pushed Guntur farmers to tobacco.

q.s: Which Andhra leader attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
q.x: P. Anandacharlu attended the first INC session at Bombay; he later became Congress president (1891).

q.s: The Telugu journal 'Krishna Patrika' was edited for decades by:
q.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika; Desamata was edited by Chilakamarti.

q.s: The paper 'Desamata' was edited by:
q.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham edited Desamata.

q.s: The weekly 'Zamin Rytu' of Nellore was started by:
q.x: Nellore Venkatarama Naidu started Zamin Rytu; Prajavani was edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy.

q.s: The Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham (Arasam), the Telugu counterpart of the AIPWA, was formed in:
q.x: Arasam was formed in 1943; Virasam, the Revolutionary Writers' Association, came in 1970.

q.s: Virasam, formed in 1970, is the:
q.x: Virasam (Viplava Rachayitala Sangham) is the Revolutionary Writers' Association.

q.s: Pathuri Nagabhushanam is remembered for his work in the:
q.x: Pathuri Nagabhushanam set up about 160 village libraries as Secretary of the Guntur Library Association.

q.s: Tolu Bommalata of Andhra Pradesh is a traditional form of:
q.x: Tolu Bommalata uses thin, translucent leather figures painted on both sides, with moving heads.

q.s: The leather puppetry of Nimmalakunta received the GI tag in:
q.x: Nimmalakunta leather puppetry got its GI tag in 2008.

q.s: In Telugu folk tradition, 'Jola patalu' are:
q.x: Jola patalu are lullabies sung to put children to sleep.

q.s: The first book on the theory of folk knowledge in Telugu was written by:
q.x: Biruduraju Ramaraju, a pioneer of Telugu folklore studies, wrote the first such book.

q.s: The pamphlet 'Writers, where do you stand?' that led to the formation of Virasam was issued by students of:
q.x: The pamphlet came from Visakhapatnam students; Virasam was formed in 1970.

q.s: The Srikakulam peasant struggle (1969), the background to Virasam, was led by:
q.x: Vempatapu Satyam led the Srikakulam girijan struggle.

q.s: The First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha was held under the patronage of:
q.x: Ajatashatru patronised the First Council soon after the Buddha's death; Ashoka patronised the Third.

q.s: Ajatashatru of Magadha defeated and annexed the:
q.x: Ajatashatru annexed the Vajji (Lichchhavi) confederacy of Vaishali.

q.s: Alexander defeated Porus in 326 BCE in the Battle of:
q.x: Alexander defeated Porus on the Hydaspes; his invasion weakened the north-western states and helped the rise of Chandragupta Maurya.

q.s: The Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama is built in which style?
q.x: The Draksharama temple is in the Chalukya-Chola style.

q.s: The Kapoteswara temple at Chejarla was originally a:
q.x: Chejarla Kapoteswara was a Buddhist apsidal shrine later converted to Shaiva use; the Padmakshi temple at Hanamkonda was originally Jain.

q.s: Andre Beteille's 'Caste, Class and Power' is based on fieldwork in Sripuram village of which district?
q.x: Beteille studied Sripuram in Thanjavur and found that caste, class and power no longer coincided.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andre Beteille is correct?
o: He found that caste, class and power still coincide.
His Sripuram fieldwork was in Tirunelveli.
He wrote 'Studies in Agrarian Social Structure'.
q.x: Beteille found caste, class and power no longer coincide; Sripuram is in Thanjavur, and Homo Hierarchicus is Dumont's.

q.s: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is implemented by the:
q.x: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission is the nodal agency for PMEGP.

q.s: The book 'Footloose Labour' (1996) on circular migrants was written by:
q.x: Jan Breman's Footloose Labour studies circular migrants in seasonal, casual and informal work.

q.s: Which is the largest Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) in India by population?
q.x: The Sahariyas are the largest PVTG; the Sentinelese are the smallest.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PVTGs is correct?
o: Kolam and Thoti of the joint list fall on the Telangana side.
The Sahariyas are the smallest PVTG.
Dongaria Khond is not on the joint Andhra Pradesh–Telangana list.
The joint Andhra Pradesh–Telangana list has 20 PVTGs.
q.x: The joint list has 12 PVTGs, including Dongaria Khond and Kutia Khond; the Sahariyas are the largest PVTG.

q.s: Roughly what share of Indian marriages are inter-caste?
q.x: Only about 5 per cent of Indian marriages are inter-caste; caste associations also act as pressure groups.

q.s: According to NCRB data, the largest category of crimes against women is:
q.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives is the largest head of crimes against women.

q.s: As per NCRB data, which State leads in cases of child marriage?
q.x: Assam leads in child marriage cases, while Telangana recorded the most trafficking cases in 2024.

q.s: Which Supreme Court case led Parliament to pass the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986?
q.x: After the Shah Bano judgment (1985), Parliament passed the Muslim Women Act, 1986.

q.s: Which of the following case–outcome pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Subhash Kashinath Mahajan – SC/ST (PoA) Amendment Act, 2018
q.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) laid down the basic structure limit on Article 368.

q.s: Under Mission Shakti, the 24x7 Women Helpline 181 falls under which sub-scheme?
q.x: Sambal covers safety (One Stop Centres, Helpline 181, Nari Adalat); Samarthya covers empowerment.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT come under the Sambal sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?
q.x: PMMVY falls under Samarthya (empowerment); Sambal covers safety.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Deepam scheme (1999) provided women of BPL/DWCRA families with:
q.x: Deepam gave LPG connections to poor women; Deepam-2 (2024) is AP's own scheme of three free cylinders a year.

q.s: Which country signed an MoU with Indian Oil in 2020 to replicate the Ujjwala model?
q.x: Ghana signed the MoU with Indian Oil in January 2020.

q.s: Which Mission Shakti component provides police, medical, legal, counselling and shelter help under one roof?
q.x: One Stop Centres (Sakhi), funded by the Nirbhaya Fund, give integrated help; Sakhi Niwas are working-women hostels.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of Mission Shakti?
q.x: The POSHAN Tracker belongs to POSHAN Abhiyaan; Palna (creches) and the others are Mission Shakti components.

q.s: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014, moved by Tiruchi Siva and passed by the Rajya Sabha, was a:
q.x: It was a rare private member's Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha (2015); the government's Transgender Persons Act came in 2019.

q.s: Which of the following statements about transgender rights in India is correct?
o: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 came into force on 10 January 2020.
The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was passed by both Houses.
The 2014 Bill was a government Bill.
The NALSA judgment was delivered in 2019.
q.x: The 2014 private member's Bill passed only the Rajya Sabha (2015); the NALSA judgment came in 2014.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides:
o: Free LPG connections to poor women
q.x: Ujjwala gives free LPG connections to BPL women.

q.s: Which of the following schemes is NOT correctly matched with its objective?
o: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana – Life and disability cover
q.x: PMKVY is the skill development scheme for youth.

q.s: The Ni-kshay web portal is used to track patients of:
q.x: Ni-kshay tracks TB patients; U-WIN records routine immunisation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a digital health platform?
q.x: GeM is the Government e-Marketplace for public procurement.

q.s: The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (2011) was restructured from:
q.x: NRLM replaced the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana in 2011 and was renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.

q.s: Under the Lakhpati Didi initiative, how many women are targeted to earn over Rs 1 lakh a year?
q.x: The Lakhpati Didi target is 3 crore SHG women.

q.s: Which of the following schemes was NOT merged into PM VIKAS?
q.x: PM VIKAS (2022) merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil; PMJVK continues separately.

q.s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured in 2018 from the:
q.x: PMJVK replaced the Multi-sectoral Development Programme for minority-concentration areas.

q.s: Which body recommended 15 per cent reservation for minorities, including 10 per cent for Muslims?
q.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission recommended 15 per cent for minorities with 10 per cent for Muslims.

q.s: Which of the following committees is NOT related to minorities?
q.x: The Lokur Committee (1965) laid down criteria for Scheduled Tribes.

q.s: The Supreme Court has held that safe footpaths and digital access are part of which Article?
q.x: Both were read into the right to life under Article 21, with reference to the UNCRPD and the RPwD Act, 2016.

q.s: The 2019 Pulwama attack on a CRPF convoy was carried out by:
q.x: Jaish-e-Mohammed carried out Pulwama; the 26/11 Mumbai attacks were by Lashkar-e-Taiba.

q.s: Masood Azhar was listed by the UNSC 1267 committee in May 2019 after which country lifted its technical hold?
q.x: China lifted its technical hold in May 2019.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the I2U2 grouping?
q.x: I2U2 is India, Israel, the US and the UAE; its first summit was virtual in 2022.

q.s: The International Labour Organization is headquartered at:
q.x: The ILO is at Geneva; Rome hosts the FAO.

q.s: Which of the following UN agencies is NOT headquartered at Geneva?
q.x: The FAO is at Rome.

q.s: Phase I of the Amaravati capital city project is funded jointly by the:
q.x: The World Bank (IBRD) and ADB lend $800 million each for Amaravati Phase I.

q.s: The AP Rural Roads Project is funded by the:
q.x: The AIIB funds the AP Rural Roads Project; Velugu was World Bank-funded and the VCIC is ADB-supported.

q.s: The New Development Bank of BRICS is headquartered at:
q.x: The NDB is at Shanghai, with its Indian regional office at GIFT City.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of the New Development Bank?
o: Its idea was mooted at the New Delhi BRICS Summit (2012)
Its founding agreement was signed at Fortaleza (2014)
It is headquartered at New Delhi
Its Indian regional office is at GIFT City
q.x: The NDB is headquartered at Shanghai.

q.s: Section 3(d) of India's Patents Act, a TRIPS flexibility, is meant to prevent:
q.x: Section 3(d) is an anti-evergreening provision, used alongside compulsory licensing.

q.s: The African Union, which replaced the OAU in 2002, is headquartered at:
q.x: The AU is at Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

q.s: The Gulf Cooperation Council, set up in 1981, is headquartered at:
q.x: The six-member GCC has its headquarters at Riyadh.

q.s: The Wassenaar Arrangement controls the export of:
q.x: Wassenaar covers conventional arms and dual-use goods; MTCR covers missiles and NSG nuclear trade.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an export-control regime?
q.x: The CTBT is a test-ban treaty, not an export-control regime.

q.s: The Pelindaba Treaty established a nuclear-weapon-free zone in:
q.x: Pelindaba covers Africa; Rarotonga the South Pacific, Bangkok Southeast Asia and Semipalatinsk Central Asia.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT establish a nuclear-weapon-free zone?
q.x: The PTBT (1963) bans tests in the atmosphere, space and underwater; the others create NWFZs.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the:
q.x: The 1935 Act (321 sections, 10 schedules) gave residuary powers to the Governor-General.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: It was based mainly on the Nehru Report.
It gave residuary powers to the Provincial Legislatures.
It abolished dyarchy at the Centre.
q.x: The Act drew on the Simon Commission, gave residuary powers to the Governor-General and introduced (not abolished) dyarchy at the Centre.

q.s: Article 371A of the Constitution contains special provisions for:
q.x: Art. 371A – Nagaland; 371C – Manipur; 371H – Arunachal Pradesh; 371I – Goa.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Article 371H relates to Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the loss of citizenship by voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship?
q.x: Art. 9 – voluntary foreign citizenship; Art. 6 – migrants from Pakistan; Art. 7 – migrants to Pakistan; Art. 8 – PIOs abroad.

q.s: Deprivation of citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955 does NOT apply to citizens by:
q.x: Deprivation applies only to citizens by naturalisation, registration or domicile, not to citizens by birth.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
q.x: Kesavananda Bharati overruled Berubari, which had held the Preamble not to be a part.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court say that the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution?
q.x: Berubari (1960) said the Preamble is not a part; later cases held the opposite.

q.s: Article 18 of the Constitution provides for the:
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
q.x: Art. 18 bars the State from conferring titles other than military or academic distinctions; Art. 17 abolishes untouchability.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)?
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
q.x: Freedom of speech is under Article 19 (Right to Freedom).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rule of Law is correct?
o: The ruler stands above the law.
Law is mainly a weapon of state control.
Courts cannot review acts of the executive.
The government itself is subordinate to the law.
q.x: Under the Rule of Law even the government is bound by law; the ruler standing above the law and using it as a weapon describes Rule by Law.

q.s: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) was adopted by the:
q.x: The CRC was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 20 November 1989.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India and the CRC is correct?
o: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.
India is a party to the 2011 communications Protocol.
The CRC was adopted by the UN Security Council.
India has not acceded to the CRC.
q.x: India acceded to the CRC in 1992 and is not a party to the 2011 Protocol; the CRC was adopted by the General Assembly.

q.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, which inserts Article 82A, deals with:
q.x: The 129th Bill provides for simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

q.s: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the 129th Amendment Bill is chaired by:
q.x: P.P. Chaudhary chairs the JPC on the simultaneous-elections Bill.

q.s: The first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission was:
q.x: The Planning Commission (1950) had the PM as Chairman and Gulzarilal Nanda as its first Deputy Chairman.

q.s: The Prime Minister is NOT the ex officio chairperson of the:
q.x: The Finance Commission has its own chairman appointed by the President; the PM chairs the other three.

q.s: Nominated members of Parliament do NOT take part in the:
q.x: Nominated members are excluded from the presidential electoral college but take part in impeachment, which is by the whole Parliament, and in the Vice-President's election.

q.s: The 104th Constitutional Amendment extended the reservation of SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies up to:
q.x: The 104th Amendment (2019) extended SC/ST seat reservation to 2030 but did not extend Anglo-Indian nomination.

q.s: Ten per cent reservation for the economically weaker sections was provided by the:
q.x: EWS reservation came by the 103rd Amendment (2019).

q.s: A resolution to discontinue a National Emergency can be passed only by the:
q.x: Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution disapproving the continuation of a National Emergency.

q.s: Which of the following statements about a National Emergency is correct?
o: Approval by the Rajya Sabha alone is enough when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
Only the Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue it.
If the Lok Sabha was dissolved, the new Lok Sabha must approve it within 30 days of its first sitting.
q.x: Only the Lok Sabha can disapprove its continuation, and the new Lok Sabha must approve it within 30 days.

q.s: The Constitution (Article 112) refers to the Union Budget as the:
q.x: The word 'Budget' is not used in Article 112; the President causes the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before both Houses.

q.s: The Union Budget is prepared by the Budget Division of the:
q.x: The Budget Division is in the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

q.s: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian State?
q.x: Sarojini Naidu was Governor of the United Provinces; Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister.

q.s: The first Governor of West Bengal was:
q.x: C. Rajagopalachari was the first Governor of West Bengal (1947-48).

q.s: The office of the Advocate General of a State is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 165 (Part VI) provides for the Advocate General; Article 76 is the Attorney General.

q.s: The Advocate General of a State must be qualified to be appointed a judge of a:
q.x: The Advocate General needs High Court judge qualifications; the Attorney General needs Supreme Court judge qualifications.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of India from Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: K. Subba Rao was the first CJI from Andhra Pradesh; N.V. Ramana (48th CJI) was later also from AP.

q.s: Which Chief Justice of India acted as President in 1969?
q.x: M. Hidayatullah is the only CJI to act as President; A.N. Ray was appointed superseding three judges, and K.N. Singh had the shortest tenure.

q.s: Justice Surya Kant, the 53rd Chief Justice of India, succeeded:
q.x: Surya Kant succeeded B.R. Gavai, the 52nd CJI.

q.s: Who was the 50th Chief Justice of India?
q.x: D.Y. Chandrachud was the 50th CJI; N.V. Ramana was the 48th, U.U. Lalit the 49th and Sanjiv Khanna the 51st.

q.s: The retirement age of a High Court judge is:
q.x: High Court judges retire at 62; Supreme Court judges at 65.

q.s: Which Article declares a High Court to be a Court of Record?
q.x: Article 215 – High Court as a Court of Record; Article 129 does the same for the Supreme Court; Article 227 is superintendence.

q.s: The Inter-State Council is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 263 – Inter-State Council; 254 – repugnancy; 280 – Finance Commission.

q.s: Inconsistency between Union and State laws is dealt with in Article:
q.x: Article 254 deals with repugnancy between Union and State laws on Concurrent List matters.

q.s: The Election Commission of India was established on:
q.x: The ECI was set up on 25 January 1950, now observed as National Voters' Day; it completed 75 years in 2025.

q.s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, booth capturing is dealt with in Section:
q.x: Section 58A covers booth capturing; Section 58 covers EVM tampering and Section 57 adjournment of polls.

q.s: Which of the following statements about adjourned polls under the RP Act, 1951 is correct?
o: All voters may vote again when an adjourned poll resumes.
A Presiding Officer may adjourn a poll disrupted by riot or natural calamity.
Only the Supreme Court can adjourn a poll.
q.x: Under Section 57 only those who had not voted may vote at the resumed poll; booth capturing is Section 58A.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General is correct?
o: He is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.
He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
The Constitution prescribes the same qualifications for him as for a Supreme Court judge.
He is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
q.x: Under Art. 148(1) read with 124(4) the CAG is removed like an SC judge; he is appointed by the President, and no qualifications are prescribed.

q.s: The National Commission for Minorities is a body set up under the:
q.x: The NCM is a statutory body under the 1992 Act; Article 350-B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

q.s: After the 2019 amendment, the term of the NHRC Chairperson is:
q.x: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 cut the term to 3 years or 70 years of age.

q.s: The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after how long from the date of the alleged act?
q.x: The NHRC cannot inquire into matters more than one year old.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of the NHRC?
o: It cannot inquire into matters more than a year old
It can only seek reports in cases against the armed forces
It has no power to summon witnesses
It cannot take up matters pending before an SHRC
q.x: The NHRC has the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses; the other three are real limitations.

q.s: Under GANHRI accreditation, 'A' status means a national human rights institution is:
o: Fully compliant with the Paris Principles
Partly compliant with the Paris Principles
Not compliant with the Paris Principles
q.x: 'A' is full compliance and 'B' partial compliance with the Paris Principles.

q.s: Which body declared six national political parties to be public authorities under the RTI Act in June 2013?
q.x: The CIC's June 2013 order was ignored by the parties; the 2013 Amendment Bill to exclude them lapsed.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a)?
o: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
State of U.P. v. Raj Narain
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
q.x: Raj Narain (1975) read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Central Bureau of Investigation is correct?
o: It is a non-constitutional body set up in 1963.
It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Its Director is chosen by the PM, the CJI and the Home Minister.
It is a constitutional body under Article 315.
q.x: The CBI was set up in 1963 by an executive resolution and works under the DoPT; the third member of the selection committee is the Leader of Opposition.

q.s: The CBI Director is chosen by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the:
o: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
q.x: The third member is the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 is correct?
o: Only public servants can be whistle-blowers.
A complaint must be made within seven years.
Anonymous complaints are accepted as a rule.
A false complaint is not punishable.
q.x: Complaints must be made within 7 years; any person including an NGO may complain, anonymous complaints are not accepted, and a knowingly false complaint is punishable.

q.s: Which commission recommended a permanent Inter-Governmental Council and use of Article 356 only as a last resort?
q.x: The Sarkaria Commission made these recommendations; Rajamannar wanted Article 356 deleted.

q.s: The idea of a 'localised emergency' was proposed by the:
q.x: The Punchhi Commission proposed localised emergency and impeachment-like removal of Governors.

q.s: The M.M. Punchhi Commission (2007) was set up to examine:
q.x: The Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was taken up at the Inter-State Council meeting of July 2016.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Punchhi Commission is correct?
o: It wanted cesses and surcharges left unlimited.
Its report was never taken up by the Inter-State Council.
It recommended abolishing the Finance Commission.
It wanted cesses and surcharges reviewed and kept in check.
q.x: It sought to protect the States' share; the Inter-State Council took up its report in July 2016.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a qualifying date for enrolment in the electoral roll?
q.x: The four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.

q.s: A candidate's election expense account must be filed with the:
o: Chief Electoral Officer of the State
q.x: The account of election expenses is filed with the District Election Officer.

q.s: VVPAT was first used in India in the year:
q.x: VVPAT was introduced on 4 September 2013 (Noksen, Nagaland); NOTA came on 27 September 2013.

q.s: EVMs were first used experimentally in 1982 in which State?
q.x: EVMs were first used at Paravur, Kerala, on 19 May 1982.

q.s: Who described Indian village communities as 'Little Republics'?
q.x: Charles Metcalfe called the village communities 'Little Republics'.

q.s: The National Extension Service, which followed the Community Development Programme, was launched in:
q.x: The CDP began in 1952 and the NES in 1953.

q.s: Under the Community Development Programme, the unit of planning for about 100 villages was the:
q.x: The Block, headed by the BDO, was the unit of planning and development.

q.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool to:
q.x: The 14th FC raised it from 32 to 42 per cent.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission kept the States' share of the divisible pool at:
q.x: Like the 15th FC, the 16th FC kept the States' share at 41 per cent.

q.s: Which criterion has carried the highest weight in horizontal devolution under recent Finance Commissions?
q.x: Income distance carried the highest weight (47.5, 50, 45 and 42.5 per cent from the 13th to the 16th FC).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a criterion of the Fifteenth Finance Commission's horizontal devolution?
q.x: Contribution to GDP was introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission.

q.s: The power of Panchayats to impose taxes and their funds is dealt with in Article:
q.x: Article 243H covers finances; 243G covers powers and responsibilities under the Eleventh Schedule.

q.s: The Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee (1995) formed the basis of the:
q.x: The Bhuria Committee's recommendations led to the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996.

q.s: Which of the following committees is NOT related to tribal affairs?
q.x: The Sachar Committee studied the status of Muslims.

q.s: Which Lok Sabha had the highest number of women members (78) so far?
q.x: The 17th Lok Sabha (2019) had 78 women; the 18th (2024) has 74.

q.s: The first State to provide 50 per cent reservation for women in Panchayats (2006) was:
q.x: Bihar was the first, in 2006.

q.s: Which of the following statements about women's reservation in Panchayats is correct?
o: Kerala was the first State to give 50 per cent.
Haryana raised it to 50 per cent in 2020.
Haryana still limits it to one-third.
The UP Panchayat Laws (Amendment) Act, 1994 gave 50 per cent.
q.x: Bihar was first with 50 per cent (2006), and the UP Act of 1994 gave one-third.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the District Planning Committee is chaired by the:
q.x: The ZP Chairperson chairs the AP DPC ex officio, with the Collector as Member Secretary.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the composition of municipalities under Article 243R is correct?
o: All members are nominated by the State Government.
The chairperson must be elected directly by voters in every State.
Nominated persons with municipal experience have no right to vote in meetings.
Nominated experts have full voting rights in meetings.
q.x: Members are directly elected from wards; nominated experts cannot vote, and the manner of electing the chairperson is left to the State Legislature.

q.s: The Asian Relations Conference of 1947 was held at:
q.x: Nehru hosted the Asian Relations Conference at New Delhi in 1947; the Afro-Asian conference of 1955 was at Bandung.

q.s: India's G20 (2023) theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' reflects the idea of:
q.x: The theme reflects Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family).

q.s: A minor irrigation project has a culturable command area of up to:
q.x: Minor up to 2,000 ha, medium 2,000-10,000 ha, major above 10,000 ha.

q.s: The PM-KUSUM scheme mainly promotes:
q.x: PM-KUSUM aims to replace diesel and kerosene pumps with solar pumps.

q.s: The Command Area Development and Water Management programme operates under which component of PMKSY?
q.x: CADWM comes under PMKSY-Har Khet Ko Pani, not Per Drop More Crop.

q.s: The Command Area Development Programme was launched in:
q.x: The CAD Programme began in 1974-75 to bridge the gap between irrigation potential created and utilised.

q.s: The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was set up in:
q.x: The NWDA was set up in July 1982; the National Perspective Plan was prepared in 1980.

q.s: How many links are proposed under the National Perspective Plan for river linking?
q.x: The NPP has 30 links: 16 Peninsular and 14 Himalayan.

q.s: In October 2023 the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference to divide undivided Andhra Pradesh's Krishna share between:
q.x: The further reference under Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act was needed because Section 89 of the AP Reorganisation Act had not divided AP's share.

q.s: The second Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal (KWDT-II) is popularly known as the:
q.x: KWDT-II is the Brijesh Kumar Tribunal; KWDT-I was the Bachawat Tribunal.

q.s: Which is the largest forest of Andhra Pradesh, home of the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve?
q.x: The Nallamala is AP's largest forest and houses the NSTR.

q.s: Most of the forests of Andhra Pradesh belong to which type?
q.x: Dry deciduous forests cover most of AP; moist deciduous occur in the north-coastal hills and mangroves at the Godavari and Krishna mouths.

q.s: The new railway line approved in October 2024 to connect the capital Amaravati is the:
q.x: The ~57 km Errupalem–Amaravati–Namburu line (~Rs 2,245 crore) was approved in October 2024.

q.s: The new South Coast Railway zone is headquartered at:
q.x: The South Coast Railway zone, promised in the AP Reorganisation Act, has its headquarters at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: India is wary of which of the following plurilateral initiatives at the WTO?
q.x: India opposes plurilaterals like the IFD and the E-Commerce Agreement, fearing they fragment the WTO's consensus system.

q.s: India's first National Population Policy was announced in:
q.x: The 1976 policy raised the marriage age to 21 for men and 18 for women; India launched the world's first family planning programme in 1952.

q.s: The 42nd Amendment (1976) placed population control and family planning in the:
q.x: Population control and family planning is Entry 20A of the Concurrent List.

q.s: Urban population growth in India comes from natural increase, net rural-urban migration and:
o: A fall in the urban sex ratio
A rise in the rural birth rate
Reclassification of rural areas as urban
q.x: The three components are natural increase, net migration and reclassification of settlements; since natural increase is similar in both areas, migration drives the rise in the urban share.

q.s: Which organisation pioneered the linkage of Self-Help Groups with banks in the mid-1980s?
q.x: MYRADA pioneered SHG-bank linkage; NABARD scaled it up in 1992.

q.s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, regarded as the world's largest microfinance programme, is run by:
q.x: NABARD's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme covered about 143 lakh savings-linked SHGs in March 2025.

q.s: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was launched in:
q.x: SGSY began in 1999; it came after the CDP (1952) and Food for Work (1977-78), and before Bharat Nirman (2005).

q.s: Bharat Nirman, a rural infrastructure programme, was launched in:
q.x: Bharat Nirman was launched in 2005.

q.s: Under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, Critical Gap Funding covers up to what share of the project cost?
q.x: Critical Gap Funding is up to 30 per cent; the rest comes from convergence of other schemes.

q.s: Under the Rurban Mission, a cluster in plain or coastal areas has a population of about:
q.x: A Rurban cluster in plain or coastal areas has 25,000-50,000 people.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the irrigation component of Bharat Nirman?
o: Repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies
q.x: The irrigation component comprised AIBP, river inter-linking and RRR of water bodies; rehabilitation was not included.

q.s: Under the NTR Bharosa pensions, fully disabled persons receive a monthly pension of:
q.x: Fully disabled persons get Rs 15,000, other disabled persons Rs 6,000 and the elderly, widows and transgender persons Rs 4,000.

q.s: Under NTR Bharosa, elderly persons and widows receive a monthly pension of:
q.x: Elderly persons, widows and transgender persons get Rs 4,000 a month.

q.s: In July 2024, Andhra Pradesh renamed its school meal scheme Jagananna Gorumudda as:
q.x: The school meal scheme was renamed after Dokka Seethamma; Anna Amrutha Hastham is the AWC meal for mothers.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a nutrition scheme of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Deepam-2 gives free LPG cylinders.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the headline targets of POSHAN Abhiyaan?
q.x: The targets are stunting, undernutrition, anaemia and low birth weight.

q.s: The POSHAN Tracker is used for real-time monitoring of:
q.x: The POSHAN Tracker monitors Anganwadi services, not mid-day meals.

q.s: Which of the following statements about saving and investment is correct?
o: Realised investment always equals planned investment.
If planned saving exceeds planned investment, output and income rise.
Equilibrium income is where planned saving equals planned investment.
Planned saving and planned investment are always equal.
q.x: Realised investment includes unplanned inventory change; excess planned saving makes output and income fall.

q.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the:
q.x: The PLFS, launched in April 2017, is conducted by the NSO under MoSPI.

q.s: According to Angus Maddison, India's share of world GDP in 1952 was about:
q.x: Maddison estimates India's share fell from 22.6 per cent in 1700 to 3.8 per cent in 1952; 1.7 per cent is Bairoch's figure for manufacturing in 1900.

q.s: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Prize in Economics in:
q.x: Amartya Sen won in 1998; Merton and Scholes won in 1997.

q.s: The first Nobel Prize in Economics (1969) was awarded to:
q.x: Frisch and Tinbergen got the first prize in 1969; Kuznets won in 1971.

q.s: Which committee used the Modified Mixed Recall Period for estimating poverty?
q.x: The Rangarajan Committee used MMRP; the Tendulkar Committee used MRP.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT estimate poverty in India?
q.x: The Sarkaria Commission dealt with Centre-State relations.

q.s: The wage-goods model, an alternative to the Mahalanobis strategy, was put forward by:
q.x: Vakil and Brahmananda proposed the wage-goods model stressing consumer goods.

q.s: In Indian plan financing, deficit financing meant borrowing from the:
q.x: Deficit financing meant borrowing from the RBI, i.e. money creation.

q.s: A high capital-output ratio means that:
o: Less capital is needed to produce one unit of output
More capital is needed to produce one unit of output
q.x: A high ratio means more capital per unit of output; low growth despite high investment points to a high ratio.

q.s: The success of the First Five Year Plan was mainly due to:
q.x: The First Plan's success owed to good monsoons; heavy industry was the Second Plan's thrust.

q.s: The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 by:
q.x: The Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body set up by a cabinet resolution.

q.s: Under NITI Aayog, the Chief Ministers of all States are members of its:
q.x: The CMs sit on NITI Aayog's Governing Council; under the Planning Commission they sat in the NDC.

q.s: The power to demonetise bank notes is exercised under which section of the RBI Act?
q.x: Section 26(2) of the RBI Act empowers the government on the RBI's recommendation to demonetise notes.

q.s: In the 2023 Supreme Court judgment upholding the 2016 demonetisation, the dissenting judge was:
q.x: Justice Nagarathna dissented in the 4:1 verdict; Justice Abdul Nazeer headed the bench.

q.s: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio currently stands at:
q.x: The SLR is 18 per cent of NDTL; its 25 per cent floor was removed in 2007.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Statutory Liquidity Ratio is correct?
o: Its statutory range is 25 to 40 per cent of NDTL.
It currently stands at 23 per cent.
Its 25 per cent floor was removed by an amendment of 2007.
A bank short of SLR pays no penalty.
q.x: Since 2007 the range is 0 to 40 per cent; the SLR is 18 per cent, and shortfalls attract penal interest.

q.s: When the RBI raises the repo rate, the first effect is usually:
o: A fall in bank lending rates
q.x: A repo hike first raises money-market rates, then passes on to deposit and lending rates.

q.s: Through the exchange-rate channel, a repo rate cut tends to:
o: Strengthen the rupee and cheapen imports
Have no effect on the rupee
Weaken the rupee and help exports
q.x: A rate cut lowers returns on rupee assets, weakening the rupee and supporting exports.

q.s: The Market Stabilisation Scheme (2004) is used by the RBI mainly to:
o: Absorb surplus liquidity from capital inflows
q.x: MSS bonds sterilise surplus liquidity; their proceeds sit in a separate account the Government cannot spend.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT absorb liquidity from the banking system?
q.x: LTROs inject funds into banks; the others absorb surplus liquidity.

q.s: Monetary tightening by major central banks abroad usually leads to:
q.x: Higher returns abroad make foreign assets more attractive, pulling money out of India.

q.s: In the public sector bank mergers of 1 April 2020, Andhra Bank was merged into:
q.x: Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank went into Union Bank of India; Allahabad Bank into Indian Bank.

q.s: Which of the following bank mergers of April 2020 is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bank – Union Bank of India
Corporation Bank – Union Bank of India
q.x: Allahabad Bank was merged into Indian Bank.

q.s: Under the FRBM framework (2018), the general government debt target is:
q.x: The 60 per cent target is split 40 per cent Centre and 20 per cent States.

q.s: The FRBM Review Committee of 2017 was headed by:
q.x: The N.K. Singh Committee recommended debt as the key anchor.

q.s: Which fertiliser accounts for the largest share of fertiliser subsidy in India?
q.x: Urea is the largest fertiliser subsidy item; the major subsidy heads are food, fertiliser and petroleum.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a major subsidy head of the Union Government?
q.x: The major Union subsidies are food, fertiliser and petroleum (LPG).

q.s: Under the GST composition scheme, suppliers of goods with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore pay tax at:
q.x: Goods suppliers pay 1 per cent; service providers (turnover up to Rs 50 lakh) pay 6 per cent; composition taxpayers get no input tax credit.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the GST composition scheme is correct?
o: Service providers cannot opt for any composition scheme.
Goods suppliers under it pay 5 per cent.
It is open to suppliers of any turnover.
Composition taxpayers cannot claim input tax credit.
q.x: Goods suppliers (turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore) pay 1 per cent; service providers have their own scheme (up to Rs 50 lakh, 6 per cent).

q.s: Export credit insurance in India is provided by the:
q.x: ECGC is the government-owned export credit insurer (its NIRVIK scheme raises cover); STC is a canalising agency.

q.s: APEDA functions under which ministry?
q.x: APEDA, set up by an Act of 1985, is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

q.s: Which of the following statements about APEDA is correct?
o: APEDA is under the Ministry of Agriculture.
MPEDA is the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones.
The APEDA Act was passed in December 1985.
q.x: APEDA is under the Commerce Ministry and handles Agri Export Zones; MPEDA handles marine products.

q.s: A Masala bond is a:
q.x: Masala bonds are rupee bonds issued overseas; Samurai bonds are yen bonds and Panda bonds yuan bonds.

q.s: Which of the following bonds is NOT correctly matched with its currency?
q.x: Samurai bonds are yen bonds issued in Japan.

q.s: Before 2022, Kurnool and Anantapuramu districts formed which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kurnool and Anantapuramu formed the Scarce Rainfall Zone; Chittoor, Kadapa and Nellore the Southern Zone.

q.s: Amartya Sen's entitlement approach to famines was set out in:
q.x: Poverty and Famines argued that famines result from a collapse of entitlements, not just a fall in food availability.

q.s: The widely used definition of food security as access 'at all times' to sufficient, safe and nutritious food was given by the:
q.x: The definition is from the 1996 World Food Summit; the 1974 Conference stressed food supply.

q.s: Regional Rural Banks are supervised by:
o: RBI's Rural Planning and Credit Cell
q.x: NABARD supervises RRBs, which lend mainly to small and marginal farmers, labourers and artisans.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Regional Rural Banks is correct?
o: They lend mainly to small and marginal farmers, labourers and artisans.
They lend mainly to large farmers and agro-industries.
They are supervised by the RBI's Rural Planning and Credit Cell.
About 56 RRBs remain after the 2025 amalgamation.
q.x: RRBs serve the rural poor, are supervised by NABARD, and number 28 after 'One State, One RRB'.

q.s: NABARD's Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), funded by banks' priority-sector shortfall deposits, was set up in:
q.x: RIDF began in 1995-96; the Warehouse Infrastructure Fund came in 2013-14 and the Food Processing Fund in 2014-15.

q.s: Which of the following funds is NOT managed by NABARD?
o: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
q.x: CGTMSE is run by SIDBI with the Ministry of MSME.

q.s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is approved by the:
q.x: The CACP only recommends; the CCEA approves the FRP, notified under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966.

q.s: To be eligible for Maharatna status, a CPSE must already be:
q.x: A Maharatna must already be a Navratna listed on a stock exchange, with average net profit above Rs 5,000 crore.

q.s: When BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved in 2016, their pending cases moved to the:
q.x: BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved on 1 December 2016 and cases moved to NCLT and NCLAT under the IBC, which strengthened creditors.

q.s: At constant prices, the largest sub-sector of Andhra Pradesh's agriculture and allied sector is:
q.x: Fishing and aquaculture lead at constant prices; livestock leads only at current prices.

q.s: The share of agriculture in Andhra Pradesh's GSDP, compared with its share in India's GDP, is about:
q.x: Agriculture's share in AP is about twice India's, while services form a smaller share than in India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's economy is correct?
o: Services form a smaller share of AP's economy than of India's.
Agriculture employs about 25.6 per cent of AP's workers.
Agriculture's share in AP's GSDP is half India's share.
At constant prices the agriculture : industry : services split is 42 : 28 : 30.
q.x: Agriculture employs about 45.6 per cent and its share is twice India's; the split is about 30 : 28 : 42.

q.s: As per the 2023-24 Advance Estimates (constant prices), agriculture and allied in Andhra Pradesh grew by:
q.x: The AE gave agriculture 1.69 per cent, industry 8.02 per cent and services 5.21 per cent.

q.s: As per the 2025-26 First Advance Estimates, the fastest-growing sector of Andhra Pradesh's economy was:
q.x: Services grew fastest at 10.67 per cent; AP's per capita income (Rs 2,94,507) is above India's.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's nominal GSDP for 2025-26 (FAE) is about:
q.x: Nominal GSDP for 2025-26 is Rs 17.62 lakh crore.

q.s: The maternal mortality ratio of Andhra Pradesh (2018-20) is:
q.x: AP's MMR is 45 against India's 97; its IMR is 19.

q.s: The total fertility rate of Andhra Pradesh is about:
q.x: AP's TFR is 1.5, below India's 1.9 and the replacement level of 2.1.

q.s: The Polavaram project was first contemplated in 1941 under the name:
q.x: Polavaram was first planned as Ramapada Sagaram (1941); the GWDT (set up 1969) cleared it in its 1980 award.

q.s: Works on the Polavaram project commenced in 2005 under:
q.x: Polavaram works began in 2005 under the Jalayagnam programme.

q.s: GST compensation to States for loss of revenue was provided by the:
q.x: The 101st Amendment introduced GST and provided compensation for revenue loss.

q.s: Tax incentives notified in 2015 under Section 94(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act apply to:
o: Only backward districts of Andhra Pradesh
q.x: Section 94(1) tax incentives cover both successor States.

q.s: The grain storage plan in the cooperative sector creates storage capacity at the level of:
q.x: The plan, piloted in May 2023, creates godowns at Primary Agricultural Credit Societies; 313 PACS in AP had godowns by July 2026.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (2020) is meant for the development of:
q.x: PMMSY (about Rs 20,050 crore) is the flagship fisheries scheme.

q.s: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) mainly develops:
o: Fishing harbours and fish landing centres
q.x: FIDF finances fishing harbours and landing centres.

q.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor runs along which national highway?
q.x: The ~800 km VCIC follows NH-16 and is funded with ADB support.

q.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the:
q.x: VCIC is phase one of the East Coast Economic Corridor, India's first coastal corridor from Kolkata to Tuticorin.

q.s: The headquarters of the Eastern Power Distribution Company of AP (APEPDCL) is at:
q.x: APEPDCL is at Visakhapatnam, APCPDCL at Vijayawada and APSPDCL at Tirupati.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a power distribution company of present-day Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Warangal-based NPDCL now serves Telangana.

q.s: Under AP Drone Policy 4.0, the Drone City is being set up at:
q.x: The Drone City is at Orvakal in Kurnool district.

q.s: AP Drone Policy 4.0 targets the training of how many drone pilots?
q.x: The policy targets 25,000 drone pilots and 15,000 direct jobs.

q.s: 'Webland' in Andhra Pradesh is the State's:
q.x: Webland holds AP's digitised land records; CARD is the computer-aided registration system.

q.s: CARD in Andhra Pradesh is a system for:
q.x: CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department) provides anywhere registration and auto-mutation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective or principle of the National Environment Policy, 2006?
o: Ending all development in ecologically sensitive areas
q.x: The NEP balances conservation and development; it does not seek to stop all development.

q.s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was created following the:
q.x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment led to UNEP.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
q.x: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997.

q.s: The sinking of heavy iron towards the Earth's centre during its early history is called:
q.x: Differentiation separated the iron core from lighter materials.

q.s: Oxygen was added to the Earth's early atmosphere mainly by:
q.x: Photosynthesis by early life added oxygen to the atmosphere.

q.s: Which mission made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon?
q.x: China's Chang'e 4 landed on the far side on 3 January 2019.

q.s: Which of the following mission–achievement pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chang'e 4 – First soft landing on the Moon's far side
Phoenix – Found ice near Mars's north pole
q.x: Hayabusa2 sampled Ryugu; Bennu was sampled by OSIRIS-REx.

q.s: If the local time at a place is 6 a.m. when it is noon at Greenwich, its longitude is:
q.x: Six hours behind Greenwich means 6 x 15 = 90° west.

q.s: One hour of time corresponds to how many degrees of longitude?
q.x: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so 15° per hour (4 minutes per degree).

q.s: The Mohorovicic discontinuity separates the:
q.x: At the Moho (identified in 1909) P-wave velocity jumps from about 6.9 to 8.1 km/s.

q.s: On the Mohs scale of hardness, the softest mineral is:
q.x: Talc is 1 and topaz 8 on the Mohs scale.

q.s: Which of the following statements about minerals is correct?
o: On the Mohs scale topaz has a hardness of 8.
In Bowen's reaction series quartz crystallises first.
Feldspar makes up only about one-fourth of the crust.
q.x: Quartz is silicon dioxide, olivine crystallises first and quartz last, and feldspar forms about half the crust.

q.s: The San Andreas Fault is an example of which type of plate boundary?
q.x: The San Andreas is a transform (conservative) boundary where plates slide past each other.

q.s: Which of the following statements about plate tectonics is correct?
o: New crust is added at convergent boundaries.
The Owen Fracture Zone separates the Arabian and Indian plates.
The Ladakh arc formed by southward subduction of the Neo-Tethys plate.
The San Andreas Fault is a divergent boundary.
q.x: Crust is added at divergent boundaries; the Ladakh arc formed by northward subduction, and the San Andreas is a transform fault.

q.s: The Grand Canyon and the Hoover Dam are on the river:
q.x: The Colorado has the Grand Canyon and Hoover Dam; the Rio Grande forms the Texas–Mexico border.

q.s: Which of the following river–feature pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Amazon – Rises in the Peruvian Andes
St Lawrence – Drains the Great Lakes
q.x: The Grand Canyon is on the Colorado; the Rio Grande forms the Texas–Mexico border.

q.s: The longest river of Europe is the:
q.x: The Volga, rising in the Valdai Hills and draining into the Caspian Sea, is Europe's longest; the Danube is second.

q.s: The Danube rises in the:
q.x: The Danube rises in the Black Forest and flows to the Black Sea.

q.s: The last stage of a temperate cyclone is marked by the formation of:
q.x: When the cold front overtakes the warm front, an occluded front forms and the cyclone dies out.

q.s: Which of the following statements about weather fronts is correct?
o: A warm front gives prolonged, light to moderate rain.
A cold front has a gentle slope.
An occluded front marks the first stage of a temperate cyclone.
A warm front brings sudden heavy thunderstorms.
q.x: Warm fronts give long spells of gentle rain; cold fronts are steep and bring thunderstorms, and occlusion is the last stage.

q.s: Under Koeppen's scheme, most of the Peninsular plateau including Andhra Pradesh has which climate type?
q.x: Aw covers most of the plateau; As is the Coromandel coast, BWhw western Rajasthan and Dfc Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following Koeppen type–area pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Dfc (cold humid winter) occurs in Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: The youngest physiographic division of India is the:
q.x: The Northern Plains were built recently by alluvium of the Himalayan rivers; the Peninsular Plateau is the oldest and largest.

q.s: The Eastern Ghats are made up mainly of:
q.x: The Eastern Ghats consist of Archaean khondalite and charnockite; the khondalite hills carry bauxite.

q.s: The bauxite deposits of Andhra Pradesh lie mainly in the:
o: Visakhapatnam and East Godavari agency areas
q.x: AP's bauxite is in the khondalite hills of the Visakhapatnam and East Godavari agency.

q.s: The pre-monsoon showers of April-May in South India are popularly called:
q.x: Mango showers help ripen mangoes; Nor'westers hit Bengal and the Loo is a hot wind of north India.

q.s: Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh has which type of climate?
q.x: Rayalaseema is semi-arid, while the coastal areas are hot and humid.

q.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched in February 2015 at:
q.x: The scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Soil Health Card scheme is correct?
o: A card is issued every three years.
The card reports only pH and EC.
The card reports 12 parameters, including micronutrients.
Its slogan is 'Har Khet Ko Pani'.
q.x: Cards are issued every two years; the slogan is 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa' – 'Har Khet Ko Pani' belongs to PMKSY.

q.s: Urban flooding in Vijayawada is associated with which rivulet?
q.x: The Budameru floods Vijayawada; the Musi flows through Hyderabad.

q.s: The nodal ministry for urban floods in India is the Ministry of:
q.x: MoHUA is the nodal ministry for urban flooding.

q.s: Chavara in Kerala is known for beach placer deposits of:
q.x: Chavara, like Manavalakurichi and Chatrapur, has monazite (thorium) and ilmenite (titanium); it is not an oil basin.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an oil and gas producing area of India?
q.x: Chavara is a beach-placer (monazite, ilmenite) site.

q.s: The Pattiseema lift irrigation scheme transfers water from the:
q.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram right canal to feed the Krishna delta.

q.s: The Gandikota reservoir, serving Rayalaseema, is on the river:
q.x: Gandikota is on the Penna (Pennar).

q.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of cobalt?
q.x: DR Congo produces about 70 per cent of the world's cobalt.

q.s: The world's largest producer of silver is:
q.x: Mexico leads silver output; South Africa leads manganese and Russia diamonds by volume.

q.s: What is India's rank in world iron ore production?
q.x: India ranks fourth after Australia, China and Brazil, and is self-sufficient and a net exporter.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's iron ore is correct?
o: India is the largest producer of iron ore.
India imports most of its iron ore.
India ranks second in iron ore production.
India is self-sufficient in iron ore and a net exporter.
q.x: India ranks fourth after Australia, China and Brazil.

q.s: Most of India's hydroelectric potential lies in which river basin?
q.x: The Himalayan basins, led by the Brahmaputra, hold most hydel potential because their rivers are snow-fed and steep.

q.s: Which State has the highest hydroelectric potential in India?
q.x: Arunachal Pradesh has the largest hydel potential.

q.s: Neyveli in Tamil Nadu is famous for deposits of:
q.x: Neyveli has Tertiary lignite and South-East Asia's first lignite-fired thermal power station.

q.s: The Makum coalfield, with Tertiary coal, is in:
q.x: Makum is in Assam.

q.s: The 'Silver Fibre Revolution' is related to:
q.x: Silver Fibre refers to cotton (Technology Mission on Cotton); the Golden Fibre is jute.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Golden Revolution relates to horticulture and honey; fish is the Blue Revolution.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a plantation crop?
q.x: Tea, coffee, rubber and coconut are plantation crops; jowar is a food grain.

q.s: The Kadaknath poultry breed, known for its black meat, is native to:
q.x: Kadaknath is from Madhya Pradesh (Jhabua).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a cattle breed?
q.x: Jamunapari is a goat breed of Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: The oldest oil refinery in India is at:
q.x: Digboi (1901) is the oldest; Barauni came in 1964, Mathura in 1982 and Panipat in 1998.

q.s: The silk weavers of historic Andhra came mainly from which communities?
q.x: Silk weaving was mainly done by the Devanga and Padmasali communities; silks were luxury goods.

q.s: In the 19th century the silk industry of Andhra declined mainly due to competition from:
q.x: Cheaper Chinese and Japanese silk hit the Andhra silk industry in the 19th century.

q.s: The Jal Marg Vikas Project on the Varanasi-Haldia stretch of National Waterway-1 is supported by the:
q.x: Jal Marg Vikas is World Bank-assisted; India's IWT cargo target is 200 MMT by 2030.

q.s: National Waterway-1 runs between Haldia and:
q.x: NW-1 is the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system from Haldia to Prayagraj (Allahabad).

q.s: The India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) carries an investment commitment of:
q.x: Under TEPA, EFTA countries committed US$ 100 bn of investment over 15 years.

q.s: The India–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) came into force in:
q.x: The India–UAE CEPA came into force in 2022.

q.s: The Borra Caves of Andhra Pradesh are located in the:
q.x: The Borra Caves are karstic limestone caves in the Ananthagiri hills, discovered in 1807 by William King George.
